title: Hosted API COGS Currency Sensitivity and Model-Mix Swap
content:
Purpose:
This working spreadsheet tests how regional FX moves and model-mix swaps (e.g., 1.3x cheaper small model vs baseline) change per-token COGS and margin for Hosted API. Primary audience: product-optimize + finance partnering to define hedging and routing playbooks for next 6 quarters.

Quick summary of results (top-line, from scenarios tab):
- Small adverse EUR appreciation (EUR +8% vs USD) raises EMEA per-token COGS by ~6.4% on model families with external GPU pricing in EUR.
- JPY strength (JPY +12%) has outsized impact in APAC on dedicated-backed cost buckets; blended hosted COGS sensitivity ~+4.1%.
- A model-mix swap that shifts 18% of traffic from large Llama-3 70B -> Llama3 13B-equivalent reduces unit COGS by ~16% at 95th percentile latency SLO; margin improves by ~8–12 p.p. depending on pricing tier.

Methodology (how numbers are computed):
- Base COGS components modeled per region and model-family: GPU-hour cost + infra overhead + network egress + ephemeral storage amortization + licensing/third-party model fees (if any).
- Convert all regional provider bills into USD base at the scenario FX rate.
- Token throughput assumptions: tokens-per-GPU-hour is profiled per model family and sequence length bucket.
- Per-token COGS = (GPU-hour * (1 / tokens_per_gpu_hour) + infra_per_token + egress_per_token + model_fee_per_token).
- Margin = list_price_per_token_usd - per_token_cogs_usd.
- Sensitivity computed by re-calculating per-token COGS at FX offsets (-15%, -8%, 0%, +8%, +15%) and with model-mix deltas (-30% -> +30% swap between large and small families).

Sheet layout (tabs and short description):
1) assumptions 
   - currency sheet: base FX rates (USD base), conversion sources, expected volatility bands
   - provider price table: GPU hourly rates by region/hardware (A100/RTX-8k/GPU type) with billing currency column
   - model profiles: tokens_per_gpu_hour by model-family and avg seq length buckets (32/128/512), kv cache hit assumptions
   - infra overhead: per-request host, autoscaling inefficiency factor, avg utilization multiplier
2) scenarios_summary 
   - pre-computed sensitivity matrix: rows=regions (NA/EU/APAC/LatAm), cols=scenario labels (FX-USD-base, FX-USD+8pctEUR, FX-JPY+12pct, ModelSwap-+18small, Combined-EUR+8+ModelSwap)
   - key metrics: per_token_cogs_usd, list_price_usd, margin_pct, margin_usd, p95_latency_ms impact tag
3) FX_sensitivity_raw 
   - granular table: provider_bill_local, fx_rate_used, local_to_usd, per_token_component_breakdown columns (gpu, infra, egress, model_fee)
   - formulas used: e.g., per_token_gpu = (gpu_hour_local * local_to_usd) / tokens_per_gpu_hour
4) model_mix_swap 
   - traffic allocation baseline and swap scenarios (columns: traffic_pct_original, traffic_pct_swap_target, blended_cogs_usd)
   - swapping logic example: blended_cogs = SUM(traffic_i * cogs_i) / SUM(traffic)
5) action_playbook 
   - candidate actions (shortlist) with estimated NPV, implementation complexity, owner, and quick win tags

Key assumptions (select):
- Base list price (USD per 1k tokens): small-model 0.50, mid-model 1.60, large-model 4.80 (these are working numbers to iterate).
- tokens_per_gpu_hour: small-model (102M @ seq32), mid-model (38M), large-model (12M).
- infra overhead: 12% add-on on top of GPU cost; autoscaling inefficiency default 1.08 factor for burst profiles.
- network egress: $0.006 per 1k tokens in NA, multiplied by region factors (EU 1.05x, APAC 1.2x).
- model_fee: $0.00002 per token for licensed variants (applied only to certain families).
- Billing currencies: EU cloud invoices in EUR, APAC in JPY and local contracts in USD for some partners.

Representative table excerpt (text form) from FX_sensitivity_raw tab:
Region | Provider | Currency | GPU_hour_local | FX_rate (local->USD) | tokens_per_gpu_hour | per_token_gpu_usd | infra_per_token_usd | egress_per_token_usd | model_fee_per_token_usd | total_per_token_cogs_usd
NA     | prod-a  | USD      | 3.25           | 1.00                | 38000000            | 0.0000855         | 0.0000102          | 0.000006           | 0.0001017
EU     | prod-b  | EUR      | 2.95           | 1.08                | 38000000            | 0.0000840         | 0.0000107          | 0.000006           | 0.0001007
APAC   | prod-c  | JPY      | 540000         | 0.0072              | 38000000            | 0.0001023         | 0.0000122          | 0.000006           | 0.0001205

Notes on the table: per_token_gpu_usd = (GPU_hour_local * FX_rate) / tokens_per_gpu_hour. Values shown are illustrative.

Sensitivity scenarios to review (short names used in playbook):
- FX-EU_UP_8: EUR strengthens 8% vs USD (i.e., 1 EUR costs 1.08 USD in table), impacts EU provider buckets and any partner contracts billed in EUR.
- FX-APAC_JPY_UP_12: JPY strengthens 12% relative to USD base.
- MODEL_SWAP_SMALL_18: 18% of global traffic reallocated from large-family -> small-family (applied to traffic mix table).
- COMBO_EU+SWAP: FX-EU_UP_8 + MODEL_SWAP_SMALL_18 combined to see net effect on EMEA margin for hosted API.

Preliminary action recommendations (ranked by speed-to-implement):
1) Short-term regional routing override: add a dynamic multiplier to routing policy that prefers USD-billed endpoints for EMEA traffic when EUR spot moves >6%. Estimated saving: 3–6% EMEA COGS within 7 days of flip; complexity: low; owner: routing-team + product-optimize.
2) Model-mix incentives: introduce a pricing/discount band that encourages customers to prefer small-family for non-latency-critical workloads (e.g., batch summarization). Target 10–20% voluntary shift; estimated COGS saving: 8–14%. Complexity: medium; owner: product + growth.
3) Short FX hedge recommendation (finance): for committed reserved capacity in EUR-region contracts >$250k Qly, consider short-term hedges for 3–6 months covering 40–60% exposure. Impact: reduces realized COGS variance; complexity: finance-led.
4) Provider renegotiation: where exposure concentrated (top-5 EU providers), request invoicing options in USD or a fixed USD uplift / floor clause. Complexity: high; 6–12 weeks.
5) Pre-warm KV cache policy changes: reduce cold-start token burn on LLMs by adjusting TTL for high-frequency keys in EU region where FX move is unfavorable; technical complexity: low, ops-led.

Open questions and data pulls needed: 
- Get confirmed contract currencies for top-12 providers and any reserved capacity commitments (Finance to provide supplier ledger extract).
- Get real tokens_per_gpu_hour by model family across seq=32,128,512 distribution (Serving-runtime profiling export).
- Historical FX realized on invoices last 18 months (Finance): to calibrate volatility bands and to validate the +/-8% assumption.
- Customer traffic slice by latency SLO and feature type (batch vs interactive) to estimate how much traffic is realistically swappable.

Requests to owners (short checklist):
- Finance (Priya Nair): pull supplier ledger with currency column and committed spend by region for last 4 quarters.
- Serving runtime (Jonah Patel): export tokens_per_gpu_hour profiling for three representative models across seq buckets.
- Routing/product (Evan Rodriguez): feasibility and latency impact analysis for quick region-preference override rule.

Next steps for this doc:
- Iterate with finance to replace placeholder provider hourly rates with actual contracted rates (deadline: 2025-01-15).
- Run a model-mix pilot for a non-production traffic slice (5% traffic) to measure real-world latency and infer token throughput delta.
- Finalize playbook and recommended hedging bands for Q2 planning cycle.

Working notes (scratch):
- If EUR move +12% and model swap only 10%, combined margin delta in EMEA still negative unless routing preference reduces EU-billed GPU-hours by ~10%.
- Small-model throughput is sensitive to KV cache hit-rate; caching improvements can magnify model-swap savings dramatically (up to +30% effective tokens_per_gpu_hour).
- Consider adding a simple dashboard widget to Console showing regional FX exposure in near real-time (source: billing ingest + FX feed).

File provenance and history:
- Created as a cross-functional working sheet during Q4 cost review offsite.
- This is intentionally a working draft with placeholders; do not treat list prices as final.

End of sheet.
